answer: A hobby that is enormously popular in my country is playing and watching cricket. It is genuinely a national passion, cutting across all ages and social backgrounds. You will find children playing it in narrow alleys and open fields all over the country, using whatever equipment they can find. Boys have always dominated, but more and more girls are joining in too, partly inspired by the success of our women's team. Even older men, like my father, follow every ball on television and discuss matches at the tea stall for days afterwards. It is popular partly because it requires very little to get started, making it wonderfully [[accessible]] to everyone. A tennis ball, some tape and a plank of wood are really all you need. I think its popularity also stems from the sense of [[unity]] and pride it brings, especially when the national team performs well. During major matches, the whole country seems to come to a standstill, which is quite [[remarkable]]. Honestly, I think it is a wonderful thing for a nation to share such a common passion. It brings people together in a way few other things can. I am very fond of it myself, mostly as a spectator these days, though I played constantly as a boy. My only slight concern is that cricket [[overshadows]] other sports, like football, which receive far less attention and investment. Still, I believe this shared enthusiasm is a genuinely [[unifying]] force, and it is a lovely part of our national identity.

followUps.q: Is cricket more popular than football in your country?
followUps.answer: Nowadays, yes, although football was once hugely popular too. During the World Cup, people still fly Argentina and Brazil flags from their rooftops, so football hasn't disappeared, it just comes in waves.

followUps.q: Do you think this hobby will stay popular in the future?
followUps.answer: I am fairly sure it will. It is so [[deeply rooted]] in our culture, and every new generation grows up playing it in the street. It is hard to imagine Bangladesh without cricket.

note: Persona fix: he now mainly watches ('both as a player and a spectator' changed); added girls and the women's team, older fans like his father, the minimal equipment and a balanced concern; added [[overshadows]].
